In this special four-week workshop, participants will explore the unique art of reduction relief printmaking. Acclaimed guest artist, Tomoko Murakami, will demonstrate how to create multi-color prints from a single linoleum block. The main idea is to gradually carve away parts of the block and print each new layer of color, with each layer building on the previous one. The course covers the entire process, from designing and planning, to carving techniques, inking, registration, and printing with both hand and printing press methods. Participants will learn to explore the possibilities of color mixing and layering, enabling students to achieve intricate designs and a wide range of visual effects. item.title: Master Class & Cocktail Experience at Carneros Resort — Sat Sep 5, 10:30 AM — Carneros Resort and Spa
item.description:
Humboldt Distillery Master Class & Cocktail Experience at POST Tasting Lounge at Carneros Resort and Spa invites guests to discover the craft and character of Humboldt Distillery through an engaging afternoon of spirits and cocktails. The experience begins with a guided tasting of three spirits while learning about the Humboldt County distillery and its small-batch approach. A master mixologist then demonstrates how to create three signature cocktails, sharing techniques and tips as each drink is prepared and served. After the tasting and cocktail session, guests can relax with an included picnic lunch from Market on Town Square. Participants will also receive two complimentary Humboldt Distillery tastings to enjoy at a future date and have the opportunity to enter a raffle.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: UC Master Gardeners - Climate Adaptation in Your Garden — Sat Sep 5, 10:30 AM — Windsor Regional Library
item.description:
This talk offers concrete, achievable, science-based means to use your own garden for carbon sequestration, food security, plant and animal habitat, and increased resilience to extreme weather and other climate change events. Leah Halper is a Master Gardener and Garden Sense consultant who helps Sonoma County residents transition their yards to use less water and support more beneficial plants and animals. She is also a UCANR-trained Climate Steward with special interest in resilience food gardening, carbon sequestration, and preserving habitat for plant and animal species at risk. Registration Encouraged: Visit Upcoming Events to complete your registration. After registering, you will receive a confirmation email containing information about attending the library talk. Learn about home gardening, pest management, water conservation practices, and more from your Sonoma County UC Master Gardeners! Different presentation topic per location.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Arjun Verma - Northern Classical Indian Concert — Sat Sep 5, 2:00 PM — Windsor Regional Library
item.description:
Immerse yourself in Northern Indian Classical music featuring sitar and tabla. Arjun K. Verma is an Indian-American sitarist and composer. Beginning with his father, Roop Verma, and continuing with the legendary Ali Akbar Khan and his son Alam Khan, Arjun's meticulous training has imbued him with a rich musicality that encompasses both the profound majesty and the exhilaration of North Indian classical music. Hailed by the New York Times as a "fine sitarist," Arjun shares the jewels of his cultural heritage in a manner that is fresh, modern, and relevant, while maintaining a high standard of traditional integrity.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: BELONGINGS: Bringing Memories to Life — Sat Sep 5, 3:00 PM — Petaluma Historical Library and Museum
item.description:

Saturday, September 5, 3-6 pm
Petaluma Historical Library & Museum
20 4th Street \(Corner of 4th & B Street\)
Registration: $30 per person

What do we do with the things our loved ones leave behind?
Join award-winning filmmaker Danièle Wilmouth for an intimate, three-hour workshop exploring how meaningful objects can become powerful vessels for memory, healing, and creative expression.
Drawing from her own artistic practice, Danièle will share how she uses photographs, letters, family documents, music, treasured objects, and stop-motion animation to honor loved ones and transform personal stories into lasting works of art.

item.title: Culinary Garden Cooking Classes at Quivira Vineyards — Sun Sep 6, 12:00 AM — Quivira Vineyards and Winery
item.description:
Join an immersive, hands-on culinary series at Quivira Vineyards, offered June 7-November 15 from 11 AM - 2 PM. Led by Estate Chef Julia, guests begin in the organic estate garden harvesting seasonal ingredients before moving to the open-air kitchen to prepare a garden-inspired, multi-course meal. This interactive experience highlights the connection between garden, vineyard, and kitchen, while teaching practical culinary techniques. The evening concludes with a shared meal paired with Quivira wines in a beautiful estate setting. Each date features a different focus, including handmade pasta, masa and tacos, stuffed pasta, global dumplings, and seasonal pie baking. Space is limited for these unique seasonal classes.

item.title: Watercolor | Building Technique II, with Nancy Ballard — Tue Sep 8, 10:00 AM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Building on the skills and confidence you developed in the first class, this watercolor workshop invites you to take your ideas a step further. Explore how a simple sketch, thoughtful composition, and expressive use of color can transform an idea into a finished painting.
We'll work larger and bolder while exploring watercolor techniques including:
Wet-on-wet paintingLoose interpretation and expressive mark-makingCreating shadows and depthEnhancing backgroundsWorking in black and whiteExploring the many variations and possibilities of mixing greens
Bring a favorite photograph, a live flower or small plant, or even a meaningful memory to use as inspiration. No matter where you are in your artistic journey, you'll be encouraged to experiment, have fun, and focus on the larger picture rather than striving for perfection. There are no mistakes in art—only opportunities to explore.
Please Note: There will be a $10 supply fee paid directly to the Nancy on the day of the class.

item.title: Henry Frank: J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition — Wed Sep 9, 10:00 AM — San Geronimo Valley Community Center
item.description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.
**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.
**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. item.title: Great Company Grand Opening Celebration — Wed Sep 9, 4:00 PM — Great Company
item.description:
The table is set for something new at the Village.
Join us on Wednesday, September 9 as we celebrate the grand opening of Great Company, a locally owned dinner party shop bringing a thoughtful selection of home goods, serve ware and conversation-starting details to Montgomery Village.
Born from the founders of Reed & James Events, Great Company is a natural extension of their love for hosting and bringing people together. The shop was inspired by a simple belief that life’s best moments happen around the table, where good food, thoughtful touches and great company come together. From intimate dinners to lively celebrations, Great Company makes it easier to gather, celebrate and build community.
Come celebrate with complimentary goodies, a special pop-up from L’Occitane and more surprises throughout the day.
Source: Press Democrat
